The bill fixes minor mistakes in federal laws that came from writing or copying errors.
It would repeal about 572 pages of outdated or no-longer-needed legal text and rename a professional accounting body.
The bill removes mentions of the British monarchy in relation to Norfolk Island and updates references linked to a 2015 reform act.

The changes affect Commonwealth agencies and users of the statute book.

The Statute Update (Autumn 2018) Bill 2018 makes minor and technical corrections to Commonwealth legislation, including correcting errors in five acts, updating references to the Institute of Chartered Accountants, and repealing 22 obsolete references to the Crown in right of Norfolk Island along with 40 spent amending acts.

Labor supported the Statute Update (Autumn 2018) Bill 2018 as routine legislative housekeeping, correcting typographical errors and removing obsolete laws. The speaker criticised the Abbott and Turnbull governments for exaggerating similar bills as major deregulation, noting the claimed $1 billion to $2.1 billion in savings were "fanciful and disingenuous."

The Statute Update (Autumn 2018) Bill 2018 makes minor and technical corrections to Commonwealth legislation, including fixing drafting and clerical errors, improving usability, and repealing spent acts, as part of the government's regulatory reform agenda. The bill was prepared by the Office of Parliamentary Counsel.
